# Built-in accounts: username sign-in, sign-up, set-password links, `graph-manager users`, Settings → Account

## What to build

Replace graph-manager's single shared password with built-in accounts (`GM_AUTH=users`, the new default; `GM_AUTH=password` is an alias). Each account is a row in a new `users` table; passwords are hashed with scrypt from `node:crypto` (no new dependency). The session cookie now carries the user id (`<expiresMs>.<nonceHex>.<userId>.<hmac>`) and the auth hook sets `req.user` from the account instead of the fixed `ADMIN_USER`, so every route's `ctx.store.forUser(req.user)` already gives each user their own data. An existing install becomes the account `admin` with the password it has today (`GM_PASSWORD` or `<dataDir>/password`), and the startup output stays the same. Add optional open sign-up (`GM_SIGNUP=open`), one-time set-password links (invite and reset, 7 days), `PATCH /api/account`, a `graph-manager users add|list|reset|disable` command (a new `graph-manager` bin in `apps/graph-manager`), a per-username failed-login limit, and in the UI: username + password login, `/signup`, `/set-password` and **Settings → Account**. There is no admin role.

Only `apps/graph-manager` changes. **`packages/graph-execution` must not change at all** (its `src/manager/manager.e2e.test.ts` still logs in with `{"password": …}` only and reads the `Password: …` startup line, so both must keep working).

### Already in the codebase (from the database task this depends on)

- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/identity.ts`: `export interface User { id: string; name: string; email?: string }`, `export const ADMIN_USER: User = { id: "admin", name: "admin" }`, and the Fastify request decoration `req.user: User` (today set to `ADMIN_USER` for every authenticated request in the auth hook of `src/server/auth.ts`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/db/`: `db.ts` (`interface Db { query<T>(sql, params?): Promise<T[]>; exec(sql, params?): Promise<void>; transaction<T>(fn: (db: Db) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>; close(): Promise<void>; dialect: "sqlite" | "postgres" }`, `openDb(config)`), `sqlite.ts`, `postgres.ts`, `migrate.ts`, `migrations/001-base.sql` (tables `instance`, `user_data`, `schema_version`). Read `migrate.ts` to see how files are numbered/picked (shared `NNN-name.sql`, or per-dialect `NNN-name.sqlite.sql` / `NNN-name.postgres.sql`) and how placeholders are written in SQL (`?` vs `$1`: use whatever `Db.query` expects; check `db.ts`/`postgres.ts`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/store.ts`: `interface Store { instance(): InstanceData; forUser(user: User): Promise<UserStore> }`, `interface UserStore { get(): Data; update(fn: (d: Data) => void): Promise<void>; reviewers(): Reviewer[] }`, `class SqlStore implements Store`. `InstanceData` holds `sessionSecret` and `instanceId`. `AppContext.store: Store`. Find how the `Db` is reachable from routes (look for `openDb(` in `src/server/app.ts` and the fields of `AppContext`/`BuildAppOptions`); if there is no `ctx.db` yet, add `db: Db` to `AppContext` (and `db?: Db` to `BuildAppOptions` only if tests need to inject one) — this task needs it.
- On first start an existing `graph-manager.json` was imported into the user data of `admin`.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/auth.ts` (all, ~170 lines) — `signSession`/`parseSession` (lines 16–38), `passwordMatches` (45–50), `needsAuth` (59–67), the `onRequest` hook (119–126), the per-IP failed-login limit and login route (105–149), logout with revocation (152–163), `/api/auth/me` and `/api/auth/info` (165–168). This is the file you extend.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/auth.test.ts` (all) — the tests to extend; mirror its `app.inject` style and the WebSocket upgrade test (lines ~215–246).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/password.ts` (lines 22–45, `resolvePassword`) — where today's password comes from; keep using it for the admin migration.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/main.ts` (lines 29–61) — `startManager`: resolves the password (line 32–33), builds the app (line 47) and prints `Password: …` (line 60). Keep those two output lines exactly.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/main.test.ts` (lines 59–87) and `packages/graph-execution/src/manager/manager.e2e.test.ts` (lines 52–69, 97–138; read only, do not edit) — expected startup output and `{password}`-only login.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts` (lines 8–24 `Config`, 26 `BaseConfig`, 90–106 `optional` + `envSchema`, 109–129 `loadConfig`) — add `GM_AUTH` and `GM_SIGNUP` here. **Add, do not rewrite**: sibling tasks add their own variables to the same schema.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.test.ts` — config test style.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/app.ts` (lines 39–70 `AppContext`/`BuildAppOptions`, 80–102 setup, 139–159 route registration) — register the new route module with one line under `// feature routes`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/test-helpers.ts` (all, 60 lines) — `testConfig` (needs the new required config fields) and `appWithLogin` (logs in with `{ password }` only: must keep working).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/reviewers.ts` (lines 10–18) — the 4xx pattern: throw an `Error` with `statusCode`; `app.ts` lines 106–123 turn it into `{ error }`. Zod errors become 400 automatically.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/is-main.ts` and the bottom of `main.ts` (lines 64–79) — how a file detects it is the entry point; reuse for the new CLI.
- `apps/graph-manager/package.json` — add the `bin` entry. The Docker image (`apps/graph-manager/Dockerfile` line 46) starts the server through `graph-execution manager`; do not change that.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/App.tsx` (all, 87 lines) — the auth gate (`checking`/`in`/`out`/`error`) and routes.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Login.tsx` (all) + `pages/Login.css` + `src/web/Login.test.tsx` (all) — the login card to change; reuse its classes (`login-page`, `login-card`, `login-brand`, `login-error`, `login-limited`, `login-footer`) for the new public pages.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Settings.tsx` (lines 173–198) and `src/web/Settings.test.tsx` (lines 1–70, `fakeApi`) — where the Account card goes and how its tests fake the API.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/api.ts` — `api()` and `post(path, body, method)` (use `post(…, "PATCH")`).

## Patterns to follow

**Naming / files:**
```
src/server/accounts.ts          — users table access + password hashing + set-password links (all functions take a Db)
src/server/accounts.test.ts     — accounts module + routes + CLI tests
src/server/routes/accounts.ts   — export async function accountRoutes(app, ctx): signup, set-password, /api/account
src/server/cli/users.ts         — export async function usersCommand(argv, env, out): Promise<number>
src/server/cli.ts               — the `graph-manager` bin (dispatches subcommands)
src/server/db/migrations/002-users.sql  (or .sqlite.sql/.postgres.sql if the dialects differ)
src/web/pages/Signup.tsx, src/web/pages/SetPassword.tsx, src/web/pages/AccountCard.tsx
```

**Error handling (mirror routes/reviewers.ts:10–18 and app.ts:106–123):**
```ts
class AccountError extends Error {
  constructor(readonly statusCode: number, message: string) { super(message); }
}
throw new AccountError(409, "username taken");   // → 409 {"error":"username taken"}
```

**Cookie (extend auth.ts:16–38):**
```ts
// <expiresMs>.<nonceHex>.<userId>.<hmacSha256Hex(secret, "<expiresMs>.<nonceHex>.<userId>")>
export function signSession(secret: string, userId: string, now = Date.now(), nonce = randomBytes(16).toString("hex")): string
export interface Session { expires: number; nonce: string; userId: string }
// parse regex: /^(\d{1,16})\.([0-9a-f]{32})\.([a-z0-9_-]{1,64})\.([0-9a-f]{64})$/  (old 3-part cookies are simply rejected → log in again)
```
The secret is `ctx.store.instance().sessionSecret`.

**scrypt hash format (accounts.ts):**
```ts
import { randomBytes, scrypt as scryptCb, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";
import { promisify } from "node:util";
const scrypt = promisify(scryptCb) as (pw: string, salt: Buffer, len: number, opts: { N: number; r: number; p: number }) => Promise<Buffer>;
// stored: "scrypt$16384$8$1$<saltBase64url>$<hashBase64url>", 16-byte salt, 64-byte key
```

**Test pattern:** server tests use `appWithLogin()` / `buildApp(testConfig(dir), { webDir, viewCache: false })` and `app.inject` (see `auth.test.ts` lines 13–36, `routes/reviewers.test.ts` lines 15–24). Web tests are `// @vitest-environment jsdom` with `vi.stubGlobal("fetch", …)` (see `Login.test.tsx` lines 11–19).

## Step-by-step tasks

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/db/migrations/002-users.sql`

- **IMPLEMENT**: SQL valid on SQLite and Postgres (split into `002-users.sqlite.sql` / `002-users.postgres.sql` only if needed, following how `migrate.ts` picks files):
  ```sql
  CREATE TABLE users (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    username TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    display_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    password_hash TEXT,              -- NULL until a set-password link is used; NULL for gateway users (later task)
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,        -- ISO 8601
    disabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
  );
  CREATE TABLE password_links (
    token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,     -- sha256 hex of the token; the token itself is never stored
    user_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    expires_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    used_at TEXT
  );
  ```
  Keep exactly the `users` columns above (other tasks rely on them). Use `INTEGER` 0/1 for `disabled` on both dialects (simplest to keep identical).
- **GOTCHA**: migrations run twice must not fail (the runner tracks `schema_version`); do not add `IF NOT EXISTS` hacks if the runner already handles it.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- db`

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/accounts.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT** (every function takes `db: Db` first; rows mapped to camelCase):
  ```ts
  export interface UserRow { id: string; username: string; displayName: string; passwordHash: string | null; createdAt: string; disabled: boolean }
  export const USERNAME_RE = /^[a-z0-9_-]{3,32}$/;
  export const MIN_PASSWORD = 10;
  export const LINK_TTL_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
  export function validUsername(u: string): boolean
  export async function hashPassword(pw: string): Promise<string>
  export async function verifyPassword(pw: string, hash: string | null): Promise<boolean>   // false for null; constant-time compare
  export async function createUser(db, p: { id?: string; username: string; displayName: string; passwordHash?: string | null; now?: Date }): Promise<UserRow>  // id defaults to username; throws AccountError(409,"username taken") on a duplicate id/username
  export async function findUserByUsername(db, username: string): Promise<UserRow | undefined>
  export async function getUser(db, id: string): Promise<UserRow | undefined>
  export async function listUsers(db): Promise<UserRow[]>          // ordered by created_at
  export async function countUsers(db): Promise<number>
  export async function setPassword(db, id: string, passwordHash: string): Promise<void>
  export async function setDisplayName(db, id: string, name: string): Promise<void>
  export async function disableUser(db, id: string): Promise<void>
  export async function deleteUser(db, id: string): Promise<void>   // deletes the users row and its password_links rows
  export async function createPasswordLink(db, userId: string, now = new Date()): Promise<string>  // random 32 bytes base64url; stores sha256 hex + expiry; deletes the user's earlier unused links
  export async function usePasswordLink(db, token: string, now = new Date()): Promise<UserRow | undefined>  // undefined when unknown, expired or used; marks it used (single use) in a transaction
  export function toUser(row: UserRow): User   // { id: row.id, name: row.displayName }
  export class AccountError extends Error { constructor(readonly statusCode: number, message: string) }
  ```
  Duplicate detection: check `findUserByUsername`/`getUser` first inside `db.transaction`, and also catch a unique-constraint error from the insert (SQLite `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_*` code, Postgres code `23505`) and map it to `AccountError(409, "username taken")`.
- **IMPORTS**: `Db` from `./db/db.js`, `User` from `./identity.js`, `createHash, randomBytes, scrypt, timingSafeEqual` from `node:crypto`, `promisify` from `node:util`.
- **GOTCHA**: `verifyPassword` against an unknown user must still spend scrypt time: in the login route, verify against a fixed dummy hash (computed once, lazily) when the user does not exist.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run typecheck`

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: add to `Config` (add, do not rewrite): `auth: "users" | "gateway"` (only `users` is produced in this task; a later task adds gateway parsing), `signup: "open" | "closed"`, and `passwordSource?: "env" | "file"` (set by main.ts; undefined = treat `password` as authoritative, like `env`). Add `GM_AUTH: optional` and `GM_SIGNUP: optional` to `envSchema`; after parsing, in `loadConfig`:
  - `GM_AUTH` undefined/`users`/`password` → `auth: "users"`; anything else → `throw new ConfigError('GM_AUTH must be "users" or "gateway"')`.
  - `GM_SIGNUP` undefined/`closed` → `"closed"`, `open` → `"open"`, else `throw new ConfigError('GM_SIGNUP must be "open" or "closed"')`.
- **GOTCHA**: `BaseConfig = Omit<Config, "password">` stays; `passwordSource` is optional so `loadConfig` does not set it.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- config`

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/test-helpers.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `testConfig` adds `auth: "users", signup: "closed"` before `...overrides`. Keep `appWithLogin` posting `{ password }` only (the server defaults the username to `admin`). Add `export async function loginAs(app, username, password): Promise<string>` (returns the cookie, throws on non-204) and `export async function signUp(app, username, password, displayName = username): Promise<string>` (POST /api/auth/signup, returns the cookie).
- **GOTCHA**: other test files build `Config` literals (`project-runs.test.ts`, `sandbox*.test.ts`, `routes/runs.test.ts`, `routes/runoptions.test.ts`, `config.test.ts`; `grep -rln "graphExecutionBin:" apps/graph-manager/src`). Test files are not type-checked (tsconfig excludes them), so make the server code tolerate a config without `signup` (`config.signup === "open"` is false when undefined) and treat a missing `auth` as `"users"` where you branch on it.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/auth.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - Cookie functions as in "Patterns" (userId in the cookie and in the HMAC). `verifySession(cookie, secret, now)` keeps working (returns true for a valid 4-part cookie).
  - `needsAuth`: also public: `POST /api/auth/signup`, `POST /api/auth/set-password`. Everything else unchanged.
  - Session check in the `onRequest` hook: `parseSession(cookie, ctx.store.instance().sessionSecret)` → `getUser(ctx.db, s.userId)` → reject (401 `{"error":"login required"}`) when missing, `disabled`, or revoked. Revocation lives in the user's own data: `const us = await ctx.store.forUser(toUser(row)); const d = us.get();` reject when `d.revokedSessions[s.nonce] !== undefined` or when `issuedAt < (d.sessionsValidAfter ?? 0)` where `issuedAt = s.expires - SESSION_TTL_MS`. If `revokedSessions` is no longer in `dataSchema` (store.ts) because the database task moved it to `InstanceData`, move it back into `dataSchema` (it is per user now). Add `sessionsValidAfter: z.number().optional()` to `dataSchema` in `store.ts`. On success set `req.user = toUser(row)` (replaces `ADMIN_USER`).
  - Login: body `z.object({ username: z.string().optional(), password: z.string() })`; a missing username means `"admin"` (keeps `{password}` clients, curl in TESTING.md and the engine's e2e test working). Normalize username with `.trim().toLowerCase()`.
  - Failed-login limit: keep the per-IP map and add a second map keyed by username, same `LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES` (10) and `LOGIN_WINDOW_MS` (15 min). Check both before verifying; 429 with `retry-after` (the later of the two) and `{"error":"too many failed logins; try again later"}` as today. A failure increments both.
  - Wrong username or password → 401 `{"error":"wrong username or password"}`. Right password but `disabled` → 403 `{"error":"account disabled"}`. Success → 204 + `setCookie(SESSION_COOKIE, signSession(secret, row.id), …)`.
  - Logout: revoke the nonce in the **user's** data (`(await ctx.store.forUser(req.user)).update(d => …)`), pruning expired entries as today.
  - `GET /api/auth/me` → `{ user: { id, name }, mode: "users" }` (a later task adds gateway mode and `logoutUrl`).
  - `GET /api/auth/info` (public) → `{ host: os.hostname(), mode: "users", signup: ctx.config.signup === "open" }`.
  - Export `issueSession(reply, ctx, userId, now?)` (sets the cookie) for the account routes.
- **IMPORTS**: `getUser, findUserByUsername, verifyPassword, toUser` from `./accounts.js`.
- **GOTCHA**: `onRequest` also runs for WebSocket upgrades and the run-page proxy (`/runs/<ws>/<id>/view`); the same check covers them. Keep the Origin check first, unchanged.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- auth`

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/admin.ts` (or put it in accounts.ts) and UPDATE `app.ts` + `main.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT** `export async function ensureAdmin(db, password: string, source: "env" | "file" | undefined): Promise<{ adminMatches: boolean; users: number }>`:
  - no users at all → `createUser(db, { id: "admin", username: "admin", displayName: "admin", passwordHash: await hashPassword(password) })`;
  - users exist and `source !== "file"` (GM_PASSWORD set, or tests) → set admin's password to `password` (create `admin` if it has no row);
  - `source === "file"` and users exist → change nothing.
  - Returns whether admin's hash now matches `password`, and the user count. The 10-character minimum does **not** apply here (`GM_PASSWORD=pw` must keep working).
- In `buildApp` (app.ts), when `config.auth !== "gateway"`, call `ensureAdmin(db, config.password, config.passwordSource)` after the store is open, before routes. Expose the result for main.ts (e.g. `app.decorate("adminStatus", …)` or return it via a `BuildAppOptions.onAdmin` callback — keep it simple).
- `main.ts`: set `passwordSource: pw.source` in the config. Startup output stays two lines: line 1 unchanged; line 2 `Password: from GM_PASSWORD` (env) or `Password: <pw> (saved in <file>)` when admin's password still matches the file; otherwise (admin changed it in Settings → Account) `Accounts: <n>; manage them with graph-manager users`. `main.test.ts` and the engine's `manager.e2e.test.ts` must pass unchanged.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- main`

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/accounts.ts` and register it in `app.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT** `export async function accountRoutes(app: FastifyInstance, ctx: AppContext)`:
  - `POST /api/auth/signup { username, displayName, password }`: 404 `{"error":"sign-up is closed"}` unless `ctx.config.signup === "open"`; 400 `{"error":"username must be 3–32 characters of a-z, 0-9, _ and -"}`; 400 `{"error":"password must be at least 10 characters"}`; 409 `{"error":"username taken"}`; `displayName` trimmed, 1–64 chars (empty → username). Success: create (id = username), issue the cookie, 204.
  - `POST /api/auth/set-password { token, password }`: 400 short password (same message); `usePasswordLink` → undefined → 400 `{"error":"link expired or used"}`; disabled user → 403 `{"error":"account disabled"}`. Success: `setPassword`, set the user's `sessionsValidAfter = Date.now() + 1`, then issue a cookie with `now = sessionsValidAfter` (so it is not cut off), 204.
  - `GET /api/account` → `{ id, username, displayName }` of `req.user`.
  - `PATCH /api/account { displayName?, currentPassword?, newPassword? }`: `displayName` → `setDisplayName`; `newPassword` needs `currentPassword` that verifies (else 400 `{"error":"current password is wrong"}`), ≥ 10 chars (else 400 short-password message); on change: `setPassword`, set `sessionsValidAfter = Date.now() + 1` in the user's data and re-issue this browser's cookie with `now = sessionsValidAfter` — every other cookie of the user stops working. Answers 200 `{ id, username, displayName }`.
- One line in app.ts under `// feature routes`: `await accountRoutes(app, ctx);`
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- accounts`

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/cli/users.ts` and `apps/graph-manager/src/server/cli.ts`; UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/package.json`

- **IMPLEMENT** `export async function usersCommand(argv: string[], env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv, out = { log: console.log, error: console.error }): Promise<number>` using `parseArgs` from `node:util`:
  - Reads the config with `loadConfig(env)` and opens the same database as the server with `openDb(config)` (+ run migrations the way buildApp/task-1 code does), closes it at the end.
  - `users add <username> [--name <display name>] [--url <base>]` → creates the user without a password, prints `Created user <username>.` and `Set-password link (valid 7 days, works once): <base>/set-password?token=<token>`; base = `--url`, else `browserUrl(config.host, config.port)` from `main.ts` (move `browserUrl` to a tiny module if importing main.ts would start anything — it does not today: main only starts under `isMain`).
  - `users list` → one line per user: `<username>\t<display name>\t<created_at date>\t<active|disabled|no password>`; `No users.` when empty.
  - `users reset <username> [--url <base>]` → new link (earlier unused links of that user are invalidated), same link line.
  - `users disable <username>` → `Disabled <username>.`
  - Errors: unknown user → stderr `error: no user <username>`, exit 1; bad username → stderr with the username message, exit 1; duplicate → `error: username taken`, exit 1; unknown/missing subcommand → usage text on stderr, exit 2.
- `src/server/cli.ts` (the `graph-manager` bin, `#!/usr/bin/env node`): `const [cmd, ...rest] = process.argv.slice(2)`; `users` → `process.exitCode = await usersCommand(rest, process.env)`; no command or `serve` → start the server exactly as `main.ts` does when run directly (reuse `startManager` + the same SIGINT/SIGTERM handling); anything else → usage on stderr, exit 2. Guard with `isMain(import.meta.url)`. Keep the subcommand table easy to extend (another task adds `agent`): `const COMMANDS: Record<string, (argv: string[]) => Promise<number>>`. **If `src/server/cli.ts` already exists** (a parallel task may have created it for `graph-manager agent`), add `users` to it instead of rewriting it.
- `apps/graph-manager/package.json`: add `"bin": { "graph-manager": "dist/server/cli.js" }` (keep `start`). The engine's bundle script copies `dist/server` as a whole, so nothing else is needed.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run build -w graph-manager && node apps/graph-manager/dist/server/cli.js users list` with `GM_DATA_DIR=$(mktemp -d)` prints `No users.` (the admin row only exists after the server started once).

### UPDATE web: `src/web/pages/Login.tsx`, CREATE `src/web/pages/Signup.tsx`, `src/web/pages/SetPassword.tsx`, `src/web/pages/AccountCard.tsx`; UPDATE `src/web/App.tsx`, `src/web/pages/Settings.tsx`

- **Login.tsx**: fields **Username** (`autoComplete="username"`, prefilled from `localStorage["gm.lastUsername"]`, wrap storage access in try/catch) and **Password**; body `JSON.stringify({ username, password })`; saves the username on success; 401 → "Wrong username or password."; 403 → server text; 429 as today. Reads `/api/auth/info` → when `signup === true` shows a link **Create account** to `/signup`. Footer when sign-up is closed: "Accounts are added on the server with <code>graph-manager users add</code>." (replaces the GM_PASSWORD text). Login is rendered outside the router: navigate with `window.history.pushState` + a re-render, or render the logged-out pages inside their own `<BrowserRouter>` (below) and use `<Link>`.
- **App.tsx**: when `auth === "out"`, render `<BrowserRouter><Routes><Route path="/signup" element={<Signup onLogin={…} />} /><Route path="/set-password" element={<SetPassword onLogin={…} />} /><Route path="*" element={<Login onLogin={…} />} /></Routes></BrowserRouter>`. `/set-password` must also work when a different user is logged in: if `window.location.pathname === "/set-password"` at startup, show `SetPassword` regardless of the auth state. After `onLogin` navigate to `/` (`window.history.replaceState({}, "", "/")`).
- **Signup.tsx** (`data-testid="page-signup"`): Username, Display name, Password, Repeat password; client check "Passwords don't match."; POST `/api/auth/signup`; server error text shown in `login-error`; success → `onLogin()`. Link back "Log in".
- **SetPassword.tsx** (`data-testid="page-set-password"`): reads `token` from `location.search`; Password + Repeat; POST `/api/auth/set-password`; on 400 `link expired or used` show "This link has expired or was already used. Ask for a new one." ; success → `onLogin()`.
- **AccountCard.tsx** (`<section className="settings-card" aria-label="Account" data-testid="account">`): loads `GET /api/account`; shows the username (read-only, mono), a Display name input + **Save**, and Change password (Current password, New password, Repeat) + **Change password**; uses `post("/api/account", body, "PATCH")`; toasts "Saved." / "Password changed. Other sign-ins were ended."; errors inline (`field-error`). Render it first inside `Settings` (Settings.tsx line ~184, before `settings-forges`).
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run typecheck && npm test -w graph-manager -- Login Settings App`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `POST /api/auth/login {username,password}` → 204 + cookie `<expiresMs>.<nonceHex>.<userId>.<hmac>`; wrong → 401 `{"error":"wrong username or password"}`; `{password}` alone logs in as `admin`; disabled → 403 `{"error":"account disabled"}`.
- [ ] Failed logins are limited per IP and per username (10 per 15 minutes each) → 429 with `Retry-After`.
- [ ] `POST /api/auth/signup` only with `GM_SIGNUP=open` (else 404); 409 `{"error":"username taken"}`; 400 for a bad username or a password under 10 characters.
- [ ] `POST /api/auth/set-password {token,password}` works once within 7 days; else 400 `{"error":"link expired or used"}`.
- [ ] `PATCH /api/account` changes the display name and the password; a password change ends the user's other cookies.
- [ ] A disabled user's cookie stops working at once; `req.user` is the cookie's user, so two accounts never see each other's data.
- [ ] An existing install signs in as `admin` with its old password; startup still prints `Password: from GM_PASSWORD` or `Password: <pw> (saved in <file>)`; `GM_AUTH=password` works as an alias; `GM_AUTH=x` → `GM_AUTH must be "users" or "gateway"`.
- [ ] `graph-manager users add <name>` prints `<url>/set-password?token=…` that sets the password once; `list`, `reset`, `disable` work against the server's database.
- [ ] The login page asks for username and password, remembers the last username, shows **Create account** only with open sign-up; `/signup` and `/set-password` work; Settings shows an Account card.
- [ ] `packages/graph-execution` is unchanged; `git diff --stat -- packages/graph-execution` is empty.
- [ ] Tests pass: `npm test -w graph-manager -- auth accounts config main Login Signup Settings App`
